FINDER F4b, PART 3i: THE REVIEW LAB BROWSER RUN FAILS DETERMINISTICALLY ON PR #965. Work on this branch only (feat/finder-f4b, now at 82766f3e, the PR head). Both reviewers passed this head; only the required `Review Lab` check failed (run 41281603236, job "Review Lab", report artifact `review-lab-report`).

EVIDENCE. browser-summary.json: syntheticWiring and apiFailure passed; rankingsApiFailure failed with `fatalError: "Timed out retrying after 10000ms: expected 503 to equal 200"`. The recorded POST /api/local/search responses were, in order: 200 (syntheticWiring visit), 200 (apiFailure's establishSelectedSystem visit), 503 (apiFailure's deliberate failed search), 200 (rankingsApiFailure's establishSelectedSystem visit). The failure screenshot shows /explore?selected=9100000000001 fully loaded with the Any results, so the page did get its 200.

CAUSE. In apps/web/cypress/e2e/review-lab.cy.ts, F4b added `establishSelectedSystem()`, which registers `cy.intercept('POST', '/api/local/search').as('selectionSearch')` and then `cy.wait('@selectionSearch')`. On main this helper does not exist; on this branch it is called twice, from the apiFailure flow and from the rankingsApiFailure flow. The first call's route stays active, so the apiFailure flow's deliberate 503 search also matches it and is recorded under the alias `selectionSearch`. Cypress counts waits per alias, so the second `cy.wait('@selectionSearch')` returns the second request recorded under that alias, which is the 503 from the previous flow, not the new visit's 200. The order of the flows is fixed, so this fails on every run.

CHANGE. Make each establishSelectedSystem call wait on its own, fresh alias (for example a counter-based `selectionSearch1`, `selectionSearch2`), so a wait can only see requests made after its own intercept was registered. Keep the assertions (status 200, renderer ready, assertSelectionPreserved) and the flow order unchanged. Then audit the whole spec for the same hazard: any alias that is registered more than once, or waited on more than once, or that an earlier flow's still-active route could have fed with a request from a previous flow; fix each one the same way, and say in your report which aliases you checked. Do not add sleeps or retries, and do not stub responses: the Review Lab uses the backend-owned review modes.

CONTRACTS. tests/test_review_lab_v3.py and other contract tests may pin spec text; run `grep -rn "selectionSearch\|establishSelectedSystem" tests` and update any pinned string to the new form, asserting the stronger property (a fresh alias per call) rather than restoring old text.

VALIDATION. In apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and eslint/prettier on the spec. Then `python -m pytest -q tests/test_review_lab_v3.py tests/test_review_lab_timeouts.py tests/test_db_isolation_guardrails.py tests/test_e2e_harness_contract.py tests/test_v3_product_journey_contract.py tests/test_svelte_platform_contracts.py tests/test_svelte_web_foundation_contract.py`. Report the results and every changed line of the spec.
